name: PRKDC (SCID)
summary: PRKDC, on chromosome 9, encodes the catalytic subunit of DNA-dependent protein kinase (DNA-PKcs), which repairs double-strand breaks in DNA and is needed for the DNA rearrangement that builds antibodies and T-cell receptors. A five base-pair deletion of TCTCA (c.9478_9482del, p.Asn3160fs*3; g.36395752_36395756del on EquCab3.0; older papers number it c.4675_4679del on another transcript) shifts the reading frame, truncates the protein and removes its kinase activity. Two copies cause severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID): a foal with no adaptive immune system that dies of infection, generally within four to six months. It is recessive; carriers are clinically normal. It is a disease of Arabian and part-Arabian horses. How common carriers are varies by country: 8.4 per cent of 250 randomly chosen American Arabians in 1998, 1.6 per cent of 244 Arabians in Iran in 2015, none of 239 at Turkish state studs, none of 33 Egyptian Arabians in 2018, and none found in a 2026 sequencing of 120 Arabians from Poland, the United States, Egypt and Syria; UC Davis gives 1 to 8 per cent, depending on the country. No link between carrier status and sarcoids is established. UC Davis writes the genotypes N/N, N/SCID and SCID/SCID. No effect on coat, build or performance is established.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: PRKDC (SCID) carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy. The horse is clinically normal and passes the copy to about half its foals. A foal is affected only when both parents pass it on.

phenotypes.name: SCID (no immune system)
phenotypes.description: Two copies. The foal has no working B or T cells and so no adaptive immune system. It suffers repeated or overwhelming infections of every kind - pneumonia, diarrhoea, lethargy, poor growth - and generally does not live beyond about four to six months.

Arabian, Iran, 2015 (244 horses, 228 of them Persian or Asil Arabians and 16 imported; 1.6% carriers, allele frequency 0.8%)
Arabian, Turkish state studs (no carrier in 239 horses; year not given)
Arabian, Egypt, 2018 (no carrier among 33 randomly selected Arabians, as cited by OMIA; a small sample)
